conviction_note: Balanced evidence: Q2's own leading credit indicators (C-M3 1.0% from 1.2%, 30+DPD 5.8% from 6.1%) and opex -27.5% point to a better Q3 credit/cost line, while the Q2 headline improvement was entirely tax-driven (pretax RMB30m vs RMB266m), the sector's funding squeeze since late June (Qifu guided Q3 non-GAAP NI -67% to -73% y/y) weighs on volume, and the last confirmed print (Q2, Aug 18 amc) sold off -5.2% on an 86% narrower loss; findings sum to -0.2, so p_up 50 and expected 0 on an abs move of 6.5% (no usable chain; scale from the Q2 reaction, 63% realised vol and a thin, post-reverse-split ADS).
bar: unsourced: no consensus EPS or revenue for Q3 2026 found (Earnings Whispers shows '—' for estimates, https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/LU); Lufax gives no quantified guidance (Q2 release, https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/lufax-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-544422.shtml). The only reference points are Q2 2026: total income RMB6,227m (-15.5% y/y), net loss RMB82m, pretax profit RMB30m; Q1 2026 implied net loss RMB612m. Every size is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest ~3.0% of float, 'rising' per Benzinga sentiment page (last updated ~Oct 19, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/LU/sentiment); Equibles July 8 2026: 6.7M shares, 0.8% of float, 4.9 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/lu/summary) — not crowded. No usable option chain: ATM legs not two-sided, skew null, put/call OI ratio 4.92 on only 438 total contracts (baseline). Stock -34% since Sep 28 (split-adjusted $12.60 -> $8.29), 3% above its 52w low, after the HK line resumed on Sep 24 (-40.8% that day) and a 1-for-10 ADS reverse split effective Oct 23 (Yahoo split event 2026-10-23). The HK line trades at a premium to the ADS (about 14-18% through October, ~42% on Oct 26).

findings.finding: Q2 2026's 86% narrower net loss (RMB82m vs RMB594m) came entirely from tax: pretax profit fell to RMB30m from RMB266m and income tax expense fell to RMB112m from RMB861m, so the Q3 headline depends on whether the tax line stays low; the operating run-rate is roughly breakeven pretax and H1 net loss widened 33.7% to RMB694m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the last confirmed print (Q2 2026, released Aug 18 amc) the stock went from $15.30 to $14.50 (split-adjusted), -5.2%, despite the 86% narrower headline loss (Yahoo chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LU?period1=1786665600&period2=1787443200&interval=1d), consistent with the market looking through the tax-driven improvement.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Q2 selloff suggests holders already discount the tax line. What is not priced is the Q3 tax charge itself; with no consensus, nobody has a published number for Q3 net income, so a reversion of the tax line to the Q1 pattern (Q1 implied net loss RMB612m) would print as a sharp sequential deterioration in the headline. If it were fully priced there would be a published estimate showing a Q3 loss.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as finding 3 (https://en.prnasia.com/releases/apac/lufax-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-544422.shtml) — the two read different lines of one document (tax vs credit indicators) and point opposite ways.

findings.finding: Sector funding squeeze: Lexin said funding providers tightened or suspended supply across the industry in late June 2026, and Qifu guided Q3 2026 non-GAAP net income -67% to -73% y/y citing tighter funding under new regulatory policies; Lufax's Q3 originations (Q2 new loans RMB51.1bn, outstanding RMB167.3bn, -13.5% y/y) and total income (-15.5% y/y in Q2) are exposed to the same funding conditions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Total income fell 15.5% y/y in Q2 and the stock fell 5.2% on that print; no confirmed earlier reaction to a volume line specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced at the sector level since August, and LU is -34% in a month. What might not be is the transmission to Lufax: Lufax funds through Ping An-related banks and its own consumer finance subsidiary (consumer finance new loans +27.6% y/y in Q2), so it may be less exposed than Qifu/Lexin — or more if guarantee-model partners pulled back. Peer proxy, not confirmed by Lufax.
findings.independence: Lexin Q2 2026 call: 'widespread tightening and even suspension of funding supply across the industry in late June' (https://www.webull.com/news/15497380558087168, 2026-08-31). Proxy only; Lufax itself described 'weak financing demand' and 'prudent, quality growth' in its Q2 release.

findings.finding: Lufax's own leading credit indicators improved in Q2: C-M3 flow rate 1.0% in Q2 vs 1.2% in Q1, 30+ DPD 5.8% at June 30 vs 6.1% at March 31, consumer finance NPL 1.3% vs 1.4%, and expenses excluding credit -27.5% y/y — which, with 93-96% of the book on Lufax's own guarantee, should flow into lower Q3 credit impairment (Q2 RMB4,141m) if the trend held; the counterweight is 90+ DPD rising to 3.7% from 3.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same improvement was reported with Q2 and the stock fell 5.2% the next session; this name has not paid for credit-metric improvement on the last confirmed print.
findings.why_not_priced: The flow rate is a leading indicator of the next quarter's provisions; at a 3% from-low price and no published estimate, nobody has translated a 1.0% C-M3 into a Q3 impairment number. If priced, the stock would not be at its 52w low with puts at 4.9x calls by OI.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 release with finding 1. No independent Q3 credit series for Lufax found.

findings.finding: Shareholders approved on Oct 8 a one-year extension of the Ping An Overseas Holdings convertible promissory notes (about US$977m outstanding per the July HKEX filing summary) from Oct 8, 2026 to Oct 8, 2027, at a conversion price of US$2.32 per share against roughly US$0.41 per share now, removing a near-term repayment at the quarter-end after Q3 and showing parent support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No price reaction found on Oct 8 itself: the stock went from $9.81 (Oct 7) to $9.47 (Oct 8) split-adjusted, -3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since Oct 8, so mostly priced; what the money buys is time, not growth. The print and call may confirm the liquidity position after the extension; the stock fell on the day, so the market gave it no credit.
findings.independence: Outstanding notes of US$976.90m per July filing summary (https://www.itiger.com/news/1180486329).

findings.finding: New CFO Jia Liu (ex-CFO of CITIC aiBank and Yiren Digital, ex-PwC) was appointed on Oct 16, 2026, eleven days before the print, after the previous CFO resigned July 25; with a new auditor (EY) and restated 2022-2023 accounts behind it, a first quarter under a new CFO carries kitchen-sink provisioning risk on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print under a newly appointed CFO in the reaction record.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only: nothing has quantified a provisioning change. If the market expected a reset there would be some pre-announcement or analyst note; none was found.
findings.independence: RTTNews: 'Lufax names Jia Liu CFO' (https://www.rttnews.com/3699771/lufax-names-jia-liu-cfo.aspx). Inference, no document on a provisioning change.

findings.finding: The Hong Kong line (6623.HK) rose 27% on Oct 26 to HK$4.70 from HK$3.695 on its largest volume of the month (647,604 shares, about HK$3m), so the HK price per share now sits about 42% above the ADS-implied price (US$8.48 / 20 shares = HK$3.30 on Oct 26), against a 14-18% premium through October; the US line rose only 5.2% that day and fell 2.2% on Oct 27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; the HK line has traded only since Sep 24 after a 20-month suspension.
findings.why_not_priced: The ADS has not followed the HK move; if the US price reflected home-market buying ahead of results, the gap would have closed toward the usual ~15% premium. The cause is unknown: it could be informed buying or noise on thin HK turnover.
findings.independence: US chart for the same dates (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LU?range=1mo&interval=1d). No news found explaining the HK move.

findings.finding: The 34% fall since Sep 28 (split-adjusted $12.60 to $8.29) follows the HK line's resumption on Sep 24 after a 20-month suspension (opened HK$8.6, closed HK$6.45, -40.8%) and the steady HK decline to HK$3.60 by Oct 22, so the drawdown into the print is at least partly unlock selling by trapped HK holders rather than a Q3 signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Resumption-announcement session (Sep 23 amc) the ADS rose 10.66% (baseline); it has fallen since.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference about the cause of the drawdown; whether the selling is finished cannot be dated. An Oct 4 article attributes the slide to unnamed 'regulatory and credit-risk headlines' instead (https://stockstotrade.com/news/lufaxholdingltd-lu-news-2026_10_04/).
findings.independence: HK chart (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/6623.HK?range=1mo&interval=1d). Same cause family as finding 6, but a different fact (flow vs premium).

Standalone Q3 2025 comparison income statement (only an Oct 24, 2025 business update with operating metrics: outstanding RMB189.6bn, new loans RMB56.9bn)
News explaining the 27% HK move on Oct 26, 2026 (English and Chinese searches)

rejected_candidates.candidate: Early-October slide driven by 'regulatory and credit-risk headlines'
rejected_candidates.detail: The article names no headline and no underlying document; only the price fact is sourced, and finding 7 covers that.

rejected_candidates.candidate: 1-for-10 ADS reverse split effective Oct 23, 2026 (ratio 1 ADS = 20 shares); post-split drift and the depositary selling fractional entitlements
rejected_candidates.detail: A mechanical event with no Q3 content; the post-split flow is part of the drawdown positioning covered in findings 6-7.

baseline_tension: The baseline gives no priced direction (no chain, no skew), and the stock sits 3% above its 52w low after -33% in 20 days with put OI 4.9x calls; the findings balance out and do not lean against that, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: FPI history rule: rebuilt the base rate from the confirmed Q2 release (Aug 18 amc, -5.2%) instead of the baseline's 6-K matches; abs_move 7.0 -> 6.5
Rule 2 (one-offs): the tax-driven finding sits below operating income, so it was cut -0.8 -> -0.5
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): Q2's credit improvement was sold on the print, so the credit-indicator finding was cut +1.0 -> +0.7
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth ~0, positioning is a weak signal): the HK premium finding was cut +0.5 -> +0.3 and the HK unlock-selling finding +0.4 -> +0.1
Rule 6 (unsourced bar): every finding was confirmed as capped small
Rule 4 (financing): the Ping An note extension was checked for what it buys (time, no repayment); kept at +0.3
